findings.title: Migration crashes when no embedding category is configured
findings.body: The category lookup unconditionally indexes the first result and reads ['id']. If embed_category is unset (its default is empty), or names a category that no longer exists, the SELECT returns no rows and this raises before the uncategorized fallback can run. This prevents upgrades and fresh database migrations on sites without a valid embedding configuration. Handle an empty result before reading the ID; the fallback query should likewise tolerate a missing setting row.

findings.title: Normalize existing hosts before migrating them
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts settings support entries such as 'http://eviltrout.com' and 'https://example.com/1234', but this INSERT copies entries verbatim and bypasses the new model's normalization callback. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match. After the migration deletes the original settings, previously working embeds and topic retrieval stop working until administrators manually edit the hosts. Strip schemes and paths during migration using the same normalization as new records.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
findings.body: The hostname validator limits the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, despite being usable DNS names and previously accepted by the host setting. Use hostname validation that accommodates valid modern top-level domains.

findings.title: Accepted hosts with ports can never match incoming URLs
findings.body: The validator permits and the normalization callback retains a port, so an administrator can successfully save 'example.com:8080'. However, record_for_host extracts only URI.host ('example.com') and compares it to the entire stored value. Consequently that allowed-host record never authorizes even 'http://example.com:8080', and its category mapping is never used. Normalize ports away consistently or include the appropriate port in the lookup.
